chunks: As for what Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa has narrated from Yahya ibn Habib:

He said: I asked al-Ridha (AS) about the most excellent means by which servants draw near to God, Mighty and Majestic, through salat. He said: Forty-six rak'ahs — its obligatory and supererogatory [prayers]. I said: This is the narration of Zurara. He said: Do you see anyone who was more forthright in proclaiming the truth than him?

This report likewise contains no negation of prayers beyond these. Rather, the questioner asked about the most excellent means of drawing near [to God], and [the Imam] mentioned these forty-six and singled them out for specific mention because the prayers that exceed them are inferior to them in merit. What indicates what we have stated — that he intended only to emphasize the merit of these forty-six rak'ahs — [continues in the following text]

key_terms.أَصْدَعَ: most forthright / most outspoken in proclaiming

ai.seo_question: How many daily rak'ahs did Imam al-Ridha (AS) identify as the most excellent means of drawing near to God through salat?
ai.summary: Yahya ibn Habib reports asking Imam al-Ridha (AS) the most excellent means by which servants draw near to God through salat; the Imam answers: forty-six rak'ahs — obligatory and supererogatory — and endorses Zurara ibn A'yan as the most forthright voice of truth among the companions. Sheikh al-Tusi appends a jurisprudential note explaining that this narration does not negate additional voluntary prayers but singles out these forty-six rak'ahs on account of their superior merit, with the argument trailing off mid-sentence as it transitions to further textual evidence.
